frame: Selenographic Mean-Earth / polar-axis (LOLA): latitude north+, longitude east+ in -180..180, height above the 1737.4 km reference sphere

grid.layout: every plane is height x width, row 0 = north edge (lat +90), column 0 = west edge (lon -180); cell (row, col) covers lat 90-(row+1)/ppd..90-row/ppd, lon -180+col/ppd..-180+(col+1)/ppd
grid.cellSizeM: about 7580 m north-south; east-west shrinks with cos(latitude)

dem.name: NASA LRO LOLA global DEM, LDEM_64
dem.citation: Smith et al. (2010), Space Sci. Rev. 150, 209-241 (LOLA); NASA PDS Geosciences Node

sources.ephemeris: src/core/ephemeris (Truncated Meeus + IAU lunar orientation, about 0.02 deg)

planes.meaning: share of the year the Sun is visible (any part of the disk above the terrain horizon)
share of the year the Earth is visible
share of the year Sun and Earth are visible at the same time
longest single stretch without Sun (power outage), L4
longest single stretch without Earth (no direct signal), L5
mean length of all stretches without Sun in the year, L6 (0 if the Sun is never lost)
mean length of all unbroken stretches with Earth visible, L7 (0 if the Earth is never visible)

stats.visibleCriterion: upper limb of the disk above the terrain horizon (horizon at the azimuth of the disk centre)
stats.ephemeris: src/core/ephemeris (Truncated Meeus + IAU lunar orientation, about 0.02 deg)

limitations: One value per 0.25 degree cell (about 7.6 km); a landing-site-scale question needs finer data than this.
The horizon is computed from the cell centre only, in 32 compass directions (11.25 degree steps), so a narrow ridge between two directions can be missed.
One year (2030) is not the worst year: the Moon's orbit has an 18.6 year cycle that changes how far Sun and Earth swing above and below the horizon at the poles.
Sun and Earth positions are accurate to about 0.02 degrees, not mission-grade.
